For 2027 entries KAIST publishes 'Spring 2027 Entry: August 18 - September 1, 2026' and 'Fall 2027 Entry: TBA'.

official.tuition_coverage_note: Published wording on the KAIST Scholarship page: 'Full tuition coverage, national health insurance, and a monthly stipend (dependent on research involvement)'. The Cost of Studying at KAIST page adds: 'The grants will cover the full tuition fee and guarantee minimum living expenses.'

official.international_eligibility: Yes - open to international applicants (non-Korean citizens) for KAIST graduate programmes
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: All departments except the Global Technology Innovation Program (GDI-GTIP Track)
official.description: KAIST describes 'a simple yet generous scholarship program specifically designed for international students' that 'covers full tuition fees and provides stipends, benefiting 94% of our international student body', with research opportunities that let most students 'achieve financial self-sufficiency'. It is awarded through the international graduate admission application rather than as a separate scholarship, and accepted candidates in matching degree programmes are automatically considered for the KGPS or KPS tiers.
official.program_type: University scholarship (KAIST Scholarship scheme, including KGPS and KPS tiers)
official.english_requirement: All applicants must provide at least one EPT score valid as of the online application deadline: TOEFL iBT 83 (taken before 21 Jan 2026) or 4.5 (taken on or after 21 Jan 2026), reported with institutional code 0195 / department code 99 (Home Edition accepted; iBT MyBest Scores NOT accepted); IELTS Academic 6.5 overall (IELTS Online accepted; One Skill Retake NOT accepted); TOEIC 720 Listening & Reading (TOEIC Public Testing Programme); or TEPS 326. Institutional Testing Program (ITP) scores are NOT accepted. EPT waivers apply for citizenship of, or a physically completed bachelor's-equivalent-or-higher qualification from an institution physically located in, Antigua and Barbuda, Australia, the Bahamas, Barbados, Belize, Canada, Dominica, Grenada, Guyana, Ireland, Jamaica, Malta, New Zealand, St Kitts, St Lucia, St Vincent, Trinidad and Tobago, the U.K. or the U.S.A.; a second waiver covers listed countries plus an English-medium-of-instruction certificate (e.g. English Lecture Certificate); students expecting to graduate from regular KAIST degree programmes in the semester before the intended course are also exempt. GDI-ITTP track and KINS-KAIST do not require an EPT score.

verification.notes: All figures verified live on KAIST's official admissions domain: scheme wording, tier amounts, the 94% coverage claim, the 2023 cost-of-study table (tuition KRW 19,118,000; non-tuition subtotal KRW 11,070,787), eligibility rules and EPT minimums. applicant_utility.summary: The KAIST Scholarship is not a standalone competition: you claim it by choosing it as your financial resource inside the international graduate admission application, and admission itself triggers the award. Officially it pays full tuition, national health insurance and a monthly stipend whose size depends on research involvement, and 94% of KAIST's international students hold it. Strong master's applicants are also auto-considered for the KGPS tier (1,000,000 KRW/month for four semesters) and doctoral-track applicants for the KPS tier (300,000 KRW/month for eight semesters).
applicant_utility.best_fit: Non-Korean nationals with a bachelor's (or master's for Ph.D.) degree confirmed by course start and a valid IELTS 6.5 / TOEFL iBT 83+ / TOEIC 720 / TEPS 326 score who want funded STEM research at KAIST.
application_readiness_checklist: Book an English test whose validity still covers the exact online application deadline date; MyBest Scores, One Skill Retake and ITP results are rejected
Register the ApplyWeb account and confirm the intended department is not the GDI-GTIP track, which is excluded from this scholarship
Alert your recommender early: the letter goes through KAIST's separate online recommendation system and cannot be edited after the deadline
If you are of Korean descent, assemble the citizenship renunciation papers (yours and your parents') or certified records for every school year 1-12 completed outside Korea
Diarise the three annual windows (Spring, Fall Early, Fall Regular) and check the official timeline page, because the 2027 Fall dates are still unannounced
common_rejection_risks: Choosing any other financial resource in the application, which removes automatic consideration for the scholarship
An EPT score that expires before the application deadline, or an excluded score type
Failing the Korean-descent rule - partial schooling outside Korea or attendance at an international school inside Korea does not qualify
Applying to the GDI-GTIP track, which cannot award this scholarship
Assuming the tier awards are automatic: department-head recommendation and dean selection make KGPS/KPS highly competitive
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: KAIST's own 2023 cost table puts non-tuition items at about KRW 11,070,787 per year (meals 7,000,000; health insurance premium 1,726,080; on-campus housing 1,400,000; telecommunication 360,000; books 300,000; travel 201,707; student health insurance association 83,000), plus airfare to Korea and visa costs, none of which this scholarship pays.
document_audit: The recommendation letter is submitted by the referee through KAIST's online system, not uploaded as a PDF attachment - a common upload mistake
For the education-outside-Korea route you need certified certificates and transcripts for every single year, not just the graduation year
Renunciation documents must cover both the applicant and both parents and must predate the application period
alerts: Entry is a year ahead: 'Spring 2027 Entry' applications ran 18 August - 1 September 2026, and Fall 2027 dates are still TBA
The stipend is not a fixed published figure and varies by college; the College of Engineering publishes its own stipend terms separately
KAIST states the scholarship rate may vary by student, so the 94% figure is not a personal guarantee
The published cost-of-study figures are for the 2023 academic year, so budget with a margin above them
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit one ApplyWeb international graduate admission application with 'KAIST Scholarship' ticked as the financial resource; the referee submits the letter separately online, and the scholarship decision is made inside the admission result.

applicant_utility.summary: KPS is the doctoral tier of the same scheme, not a separate competition: you are considered by selecting the KAIST scholarship as your financial resource, and only applicants the department head recommends and the college dean selects actually receive it. It pays full tuition plus 300,000 KRW per month for eight regular semesters, and integrated Master's-Ph.D. students start receiving it only when the doctoral phase begins. Treat any 'fully funded' label with caution - the official page publishes tuition and the stipend only, with no airfare, travel or insurance benefit.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Research-strong applicants to Ph.D. or Master's-Ph.D. Integrated programmes whose record can carry a competitive departmental nomination inside KAIST's admission process.

Integrated-programme applicants expecting payment from year one: support begins only at the start of the Ph.D. phase
Selecting a different financial resource, which silently removes KPS consideration
An English test score that is invalid on the application deadline date or an excluded score type (MyBest, One Skill Retake, ITP)
